string.text: Access card to the control system of the main module of the emitter.

This crumpled pile of incomprehensible documents and newspaper clippings clearly intrigued its owner. Tucked among them is a school notebook, filled with jaggy handwriting of an unknown author. 
 
The writing is riddled with errors, constantly changes topics, and presents a conspiracy theory about a certain group of “scienters” who allegedly developed psychotronic weapons back in the USSR and are now using them to rule the world. 
 
The author believes that these “scienters”, who in their view are simultaneously humanists, idealists, and self-serving eminences grises, have accidentally created the Zone. And to this day, they allegedly continue to work in the depths of the fourth unit of the Chernobyl NPP, enforcing their will upon the rulers of states. 
 
This pile of waste paper might be of interest to some traders.
An unknown device with the inscription “Z-ITCh-12” on the rim. \nLooks broken, but might be of interest to some scientists.
A prototype of special equipment. In theory, it is capable of protecting the carrier from the lethal effects of the emissions. \nService life of the device is very limited.

A prototype of special equipment that measures anomalous activity during the active phase of the emission. \nTo activate, deploy the device in the open field during the intermediate phase of the emission.

A log found in the underground chambers under the site adjacent to the “Rostok” factory, which contains data on shipments of certain “biomaterials” for unknown purposes. \nMight be of interest to Snitch.

Report on the Tests of the Psychoemotional Correction Emitter. 
 
1. The tests conducted on animals and human subjects, specifically the ones placed in an induced coma or the ones with cognitive disabilities were successful. Full control over the subjects was achieved. 
 
2. Tests on healthy human subjects were less successful. However, we’ve managed to moderately affect the subjects’ consciousness and indoctrinate them with simple programs, which they’ve successfully executed. 
 
3. Increasing the power may lead to negative side effects, notably: increased aggression and an inability to follow the commands specified by the programs. 
 
May 10, 2005

These documents belonged to a research team and contain data from all kinds of measurements and a briefing sheet: 
 
”At Colonel's request, I'm writing down the further plan of action 'so you, stupid eggheads, don't get lost': we will enter the Sarcophagus from the northern side, then pass through the turbine hall to the reactor, where, according to the data, the source of psi-emission is located. After taking the measurements, we must notify Colonel as the team leader and thereafter follow his instructions without question. 
 
Just need to make sure we finish up before the emission.”

A worn-down document with ink blurred by moisture, rendering large parts of the text undecipherable: \n \n“…which led to a conflict between the group responsible for developing the psychotronic suppression emitter and the heads of the “Barrier” Project. The final straw was one of the project head’s reports, which unequivocally hinted at subjecting the scientific staff to effects of the low-power mobile emitters in order to improve their work capacity and maintain high morale within the team. Shortly after that, following actions were taken in order to…”

A worn-down document with ink blurred by moisture, rendering large parts of the text undecipherable: 
 
“ORDER 
on the installation and equipment start-up in the Pripyat area
 
In order to ensure an uninterrupted operating schedule, from 21:00 to 23:00…”

In addition to Middleman’s personal documents, the folder contains a notebook page that seems to have been torn out of the diary of the legendary stalker Journalist: 
 
“Gunslinger says he no longer trusts the scientists from Yantar. Something changed in him after the trip to the Center. He talked about the strange things that happen there and suggested we go together next time. I agreed — someone needs to watch his back now that he was wounded. 
 
But first we need to visit the Dark Valley. Snitch reported that there was something interesting for us there.”
 
“This raid into the Valley was almost our last. My intuition tells me - it was a trap. The military were waiting for us at the exit of the complex. Without Gunslinger’s help I wouldn’t have survived that rendezvous. 
We found what we were searching for, but there was no information on the Monolith there. Yes, some dubious genetic research was conducted there by the “Department of Bio-breeding and Eugenics” (what a name), but that’s of no interest to us. 
 
It seems I have no choice; I’ll have to turn to the eggheads from Yantar. Maybe they have some info. And then, I’ll head North. I’ve become just like Gunslinger. I trust nobody.”

The owner of this PDA had a habit of recording his thoughts on a voice recorder, but only the last entry is of interest: \n”I seized the container from Middleman. He forced me to do it the hard way. Ah, whatever, what’s done is done… I just realized that the container is not so simple. It’s locked with a code. Damn, I need to… I need to go back… I need to go back to the meeting place and… maybe I’ll find a way to open it. And then… then it’ll just be a case for small.”
Note from Mope to Sanya Hog

Middleman, I'm looking for Journalist. I have what he's looking for. I hear you know how to find him. I'll be waiting in the apartment building, the one on the south side, opposite the school. Come alone. \nMesser.

Amidst the array of corrupted, unreadable data, an almost intact message stands out: \n \n”And one more thing. The lab has an exit t%4K;=/9JK*-;NJ(N21owever, according to some reports, the entrance there is locked from the inside. Check it out, if possible, but prioritize taking the measurements above all.”

The owner of this PDA didn't bother with scouring his emails or maintaining secrecy. Among the many irrelevant senders, the owner of the “Stalker” bar, Rat, stands out: \n \n“He's heading North. Track his route to the Center, but don't bother going to Pripyat—it's a deathtrap. If he wants to pass through the city, then to hell with him; the military will finish him off.”
This PDA is locked. Some expert assistance is required to hack it.

List of extracted emails: 
 
“The subject has discovered fragments 1 and 3. Moving out now to sector 28.” 
 
“To units “White” and “Green”: Sector 26 has been assigned as the extraction point.” 
 
“To unit “Blue”: Three samples of anomalous formations #24 have been found in sector 03: near the boiler-house; near the water tower; near the destroyed building in the village.” 
 
“To all units: a reserve weapons cache has been prepared in the Red Forest; the geo-tag is attached to the message. Use only in case of emergency.” 
 
“Note to self: contact Major about the subject.”

A typewritten sheet of paper with a marginal note: “The access code to the airlock is 2565.” 
 
”Deliver in person. 
To the Director of the “Rostok” factory, M.V. Petrov. 
 
 As per your instructions, access from the factory's premises to the special zone has been restricted; the installation of the armored door has been completed. The following have been sent to the lower levels of the workshops: a batch of gas masks and work clothes—140 sets; marked boxes—3 pcs. 
 
Meanwhile, I highly anticipate a personal meeting with you. Although you asked me not to question your decisions, I still believe I should be informed of the destination of the incoming train cars. They are clearly coming from the city via the route under the lake, but why such secrecy? 
 
Please understand that my job requires me to be prepared for the unexpected; I would much prefer to not jeopardize my career over this matter. 
Sincerely, 
Operations Manager of the “Rostok” Factory 
O.D. Nikolayev 
February 25, 2005”
A gravitational sledgehammer, most likely created by the Burers. Snitch asked me to keep it safe and sound.
An experimental prototype capable of detecting the contamination of biological material by the psi-emission. \nTo activate, aim the device at the target and initiate a scan.

Damn, how did I get myself into such a mess. I shouldn't have gone to the base of those “gray brothers” lunatics. Well, at least they didn't take my notebook and pen, and they do feed me. But why are they even doing that? \n \nWell, it doesn't really matter. What matters is that the “Winds of Madness” must be somewhere close. But first, I need to get out. My chance will definitely come and I won’t miss it.
Personal access card of a research group staff member.
An experimental prototype that protects the wearer from the fatal effects of the apparitions. Ineffective against other forms of psi-emissions.
A device that captures and collects the parasite’s spores for subsequent analysis. \nTo activate, place the device near the source of the spores.

The unknown owner has preserved this folder as best as he could; the paper inside is almost as good as new. Among the many incomprehensible and illiterate entries, the meaning of which is likely only known to the author, one catches the eye with some familiar words: 
 
“Scienters. They are to blame for everything. The four main ones are now in an induced coma, and if I'm not mistaken, and I am not, they control not only everything. The Zone, the City, the not-Zone, the not-City—they control everything. 
 
No, I can't be fooled. I understand everything. I'm not a fool, not a simpleton, not a scienter, not a soldier, not a fanatic, not a journalist, not a doctor, not a gunslinger. 
 
But He knows the code. He wrote it down, wrote it down precisely. And hid it securely in a hiding place. Rostok. That’s where I saw it, underground. Just like in the dream, but in reality.”

A thick folder titled: “Documentation for a protection device to be used in conditions of elevated background psi-emission.” \n \nSurprisingly, all the pages remained intact. In the margins of the reports, neatly and evenly written notes were made in pencil, persistently pushing for the reduction of power consumption of the primary unit which would allow to improve the device's mobility.

A worn-down folder titled “Documentation for the Scanner of the Bioelectrical Activity of the Brains of Psionic Mutants.” \n \nFrom reading the surviving pages, it can be concluded that the scanner is capable of locating psionic mutants based on the unique rhythm of their brain activity.

An old, yellowed folder in a blue cover titled “Documentation for the Radiation-Protection Suit.” 
 
Inside, in addition to the suit's schematics, are instructions for its use and some documents from the supplier “the Radiation Safety Research Institute”. 
 
According to the documents, the suit features a closed-cycle respiratory system and a new-generation insulating coating, which partially stops the flow of hot particles. However, the safety tests have revealed certain issues with the suit's mobility and resistance to mechanical damage.

A recently printed folder titled “Documentation for Experimental Military-grade Software for Expeditionary Units.” 
 
Inside is documentation for specialized software installed onto the PDAs of military stalker expeditionary units. This software scans the area within a 50-meter radius around the user for the presence of the PDA signals. 
 
Then, based on the information obtained from the scanned PDA, as well as the messages about the owner from the stalker network, the software determines the owner's faction affiliation, reputation in the stalker community, and the expected attitude toward the user, and forms a short dossier.
A hefty container with unknown contents.

The data on this PDA is severely damaged; only the last entry is partially readable: 
 
“/0xF9A%/#A's accumulator is almost out of charge; I think this is the last entry. I don't know how many days I've been stuck here, and I don't know how to get out, but I can hear sounds! As if people are walking behind the wall. I kept shouting at them till my voice gave out, but it was no use; either they couldn't hear me, or they were ignoring me. 
 
But before that I heard that guy from the death truck slipping me something. I’m here because of him! Oh well, once I get out, I'll tell everyone. About him, and about that Major... they thought I didn't know, haha. You will get your dues! All of you! I just need to get out before the food runs out. Gunslinger said, that in ord;’^%\F?+/C6”

An old, yellowed folder, some of the pages inside crumble at the slightest touch, others are barely legible. 
 
From what’s been read, it can be concluded that the primary goal of the “C-Consciousness Project” was to create a unified consciousness capable of exerting psychotronic influence on those around it. Subsequently, it was intended to use this “C-Consciousness” to influence various political authorities, the masses, and certain individuals. 
 
How the scientists planned to control this “C-Consciousness” is not specified; perhaps that information has been lost along with the pages that crumbled into dust.

An old, yellowed folder, soaked with moisture. From the surviving pages, it can be concluded that this folder contains data on experiments that have created the psionic mutants known as controllers. 
 
Without the help of a geneticist it’s hardly possible to tell head or tails of what these experiments were exactly, but one thing is certain: the controllers are the result of human experimentation. 
 
Excerpt from the documents: “These mutants are tall, have an asthenic build and keeled chest deformity. A genetically determined disorder of the metabolism of the sulfur-containing amino acid methionine (GCM) is caused by a block in the enzyme ?-cystathionine synthase. Homocystinuria (HCU) is characterized by focal neurological symptoms, ectopia lentis, skeletal deformities, thromboembolism, and cardiovascular pathology.”
Note from the lab under the Generators

A strange note, the author of which seemingly tried to resist the force controlling him. 
 
”You are the one who will stop them. They control you, but as you write this, as you read this, you are... it doesn't matter what your name is, it doesn't matter if you can remember what you’re called, what matters is that you are the one who will stop them. 
 
All you have to do is pull the switches. Five bodies, five switches, five little jobs to do. Four are asleep, one is awake, but he has other things to worry about besides you.
 
Pull yourself together and remember. You are the one who will stop them. 
 
And I am The One Who Controls You.”

Messer, I’m sorry. I've remembered everything. I dedicated my entire life to science, I believed in progress and its benefit to humanity, I set great goals for myself, but now I can see the consequences of my actions. 
 
I'm sorry You are left to live in this "brave new world" we’ve created. I can't fix my mistakes, but I can help you. I’ve left some notes on the documents about the "Winds of Madness"; I'm sure they'll be useful to you. 
 
Please forgive me for my actions, but I can no longer live peacefully with myself. Go North, Messer, there you will find all the answers. 
 
Gorbovsky A.N.
Documents on the “Winds of Madness” with a note

There was clearly an attempt to destroy these documents; traces of soot are visible on the cover, and the corners of the pages are blackened. 
 
The cover now contains a note from Professor Gorbovsky: “Thanks to these papers, I was able to calculate the exact cooling time for the emitter — from 21:00 to 23:00. During the cooling phase, the emitter operates at low power, so you will still need proper psi-protection. Once you make your way to the maintenance lab, you’ll be able to disable it. Good luck.” 
 
The folder contains technical documents for a certain “Kaymanov emitter” and a draft of the letter addressed to a certain V. M. Chubko.
 
”I’ve attended the testing of the Kaymanov emitter today. Not only were the drugs not distributed properly, but the “biological material” were wandering around the complex completely unguarded! An utter disregard for safety regulations! 
 
And the emitter itself is completely useless; not only the equipment and cooling system costs are astronomical, it also requires a whole NPP to be nearby to operate! So, mobility is out of the question, and if the interlock system overheats the entire device will spiral out of control and begin brainwashing everyone in the vicinity indiscriminately! 
 
I'm already studying the blueprints (don't ask me how I got them; you won't believe it). I'll send them to you along with this letter so you can see for yourself. 
 
If you want a reliable solution to the foreign elements for security of the Central Lab, use our unit instead. 
 
However, the choice is yours. If you want to have a problematic emitter right next to you, go ahead, Vadim Mikhailovich, but I will not be responsible for the consequences. Next time, I'll file an official complaint to the Group for review.
 
Prikhodko P.S. 
May 6, 2005”

A note from Professor Gorbovsky: “Thanks to these papers, I was able to calculate the exact cooling time for the emitter — from 21:00 to 23:00. During the cooling phase, the emitter operates at low power, so you will still need proper psi-protection. Once you make your way to the maintenance lab, you’ll be able to disable it. Good luck.”
A PDA containing information on the location of a cache with documents on the “Psi-helmet” device.

An unremarkable-looking folder, but its contents are quite remarkable. Inside are laminated sheets with instructions for assembling the “Psi helmet” device, as well as associated documentation. Each page is meticulously arranged, ensuring it can be understood by a knowledgeable specialist. \n \nAccording to the numerous notes and attached experimental results, assembling such a device would require some rare and difficult-to-manufacture components, as well as certain degree of knowledgeability of neurobiology and cybernetics to precisely tune it to the specifics of the source of psi-emission.
A crate marked with an emblem of the “Duty” faction.

There was clearly an attempt to destroy these documents; traces of soot are visible on the cover, and the corners of the pages are blackened. The folder contains technical documents for a certain “Kaymanov emitter” and a draft of the letter addressed to a certain V. M. Chubko.
 
”I’ve attended the testing of the Kaymanov emitter today. Not only were the drugs not distributed properly, but the “biological material” were wandering around the complex completely unguarded! An utter disregard for safety regulations! 
 
And the emitter itself is completely useless; not only the equipment and cooling system costs are astronomical, it also requires a whole NPP to be nearby to operate! So, mobility is out of the question, and if the interlock system overheats the entire device will spiral out of control and begin brainwashing everyone in the vicinity indiscriminately! 
 
I'm already studying the blueprints (don't ask me how I got them; you won't believe it). I'll send them to you along with this letter so you can see for yourself. 
 
If you want a reliable solution to the foreign elements for security of the Central Lab, use our unit instead. 
 
However, the choice is yours. If you want to have a problematic emitter right next to you, go ahead, Vadim Mikhailovich, but I will not be responsible for the consequences. Next time, I'll file an official complaint to the Group for review. 
 
Prikhodko P.S. 
May 6, 2005”
The key to the safe at the “Sin” faction's base.
Boots made of a special material that can protect the wearer from the aggressive acidic environment of Lake Yantar.
This PDA is locked. Some expert assistance is required to hack it.

Among the irrelevant correspondence, personal notes, and bunch of fantasy books, there's one notable entry: 
 
“The day before yesterday, I’ve ran into Journalist. I had to drag him back to my hut to get him back on his feet. The artifact I was saving for a rainy day had to be used for that, but it is what it is. Gotta stay out of trouble till I find a replacement. 
 
As Journalist began to recover, he mentioned that he was being pursued, but didn't say by whom. Today we bid our farewells — he's headed somewhere North, maybe planning to meet his informants there. 
 
Before leaving, he asked if I'd been to the archives of the local research institute. He was interested in documents concerning the delivery of specialized equipment to some weird laboratory “ZX-10”. If I’m in the area — I'll look for it, then pass it on to Journalist whenever we meet again."

Someone's diary. The entries are undated and barely legible, the author's handwriting is messy, and the spelling leaves much to be desired. 
 
According to the first entries, the author hid some important materials in a briefcase under the bathtub somewhere in Bright Beam, next to a flat occupied by some scientist. Then the author set off for the “Rostok” factory through the city's catacombs and got lost. By paths unknown to himself, he traversed territories blocked by the psi-emissions of the "Winds of Madness". The last entry reads: 
 
“I’ve managed on my own. On my own! Without scienters, without the military, without gunslingers, and without journalists. And I don't need any doctors either, and I don't need any treatment! I've walked paths they never dreamed of; the Zone itself led me! 
 
This here is their lair, from there they rule the Zone, and rule the not-Zone, and rule everything! But they won't be able to keep calling themselves the kings of the world for long. The end is near! The Zone will be free!”

Most of the pages are blurred due to a contact with decomposing corpse, but some of the entries are legible. 
 
”April 2, 2012, 18:23. Signed up for an expedition to the city; was promised an NDP suit as a reward. It's high time to trade in my old suit for something better. 
 
April 3, 2012, 12:07. Made it to the Freedom base. Only Chrome and a few of his guys were there. He warned me that the zombies go wild before the blowout, and it's best to hide somewhere an hour or two before. Well, I'll keep that in mind. 
 
April 3, 2012, 23:40. Finally found that fucking flat the egghead was talking about. I’ve replaced the battery, so might as well spend the night here. The door switch works, so the apartment should be safe. 
 
April 4, 2012, 03:14. The noise woke me up, it’s the fucking zombies banging on the door. Hopefully, they’ll get tired of it and fuck away by the morning. 
 
April 4, 2012, 08:45. They didn't leave, the fuckers can sense me. Fucking hell, what am I supposed to do now? PDA is dead, so I can't even call for help. And I was gonna buy a spare accumulator. 
 
April 4, 2012, ... Yeah, that was a bad fucking idea. I tried to open the door, but fat fucking chance, one of the rotters even managed to bite through my suit. 
 
April 4, 2012, ... The wound is covered in white foam, fuck. 
 
April 4, 2012, ... It's getting dark. Just this blinking fucking light bulb and the howling of the zombies. The wound hurts, it's covered in ulcers. Why did I ever sign up for this? 
 
April 5, 2012, … It's dawn. The door won't budge at all, but at least the brainless fucks have stopped the pounding. They’re just standing there, and muttering some nonsense. My head is buzzing, there's a ringing in my ears, I’m freezing. Infection? 
 
April _, 2012, … I’ve kept shouting out the window till my voice went hoarse, tried firing some shots up the sky, but no one answered. 
 
___ _,____, … The ringing in my ears isn't due to infection. The brain-fucker is hiding somewhere nearby. I heard him in my head, talking some dumb shit. That's why the brainless fucks are crowding there, he ordered them to. I don't know why the fuck he’s been playing with me, but I’ve had enough. If anyone finds my fucking body, take whatever you want. And tell that old fuck Gorbovsky to fuck himself. 
 
Buffalo”
An experimental device that protects the wearer from the powerful psi-emission of the psionic mutants by imitating the brain wave frequency of the zombified.
An experimental device capable of luring out a rare mutant living in the swamps of the city of Bright Beam. \nTo activate, place the device in the designated area.
A box of ammunition that must be given to Ferret.
A heavy backpack with unknown content that must be delivered to Toad.

An old, blood-soaked diary found in the cabin of a diesel locomotive. The cover is signed “Navidson’s Record”.
 
The blood has washed away the ink; only the last entry is fully legible. Judging by its absurd content, the author tried to hide from the blowout, but it was already too late.
 
“The voices still swirl in the maze of the cavities of my skull. They don't want to come out. They ask me to look out the window, to see what's left. There's Nothing there. Nothing. But I drown them out, because I'll lose my mind if I look out. There's the Void out there. No colour and no space. Who will remain in their right mind when they see the Void? No one. There's nothing there. There's only the house inside of me, and I'm inside that house. The endless house older than the time itself. And on the outside, there's nothing. Pure nothingness. The Void. Sometimes I hear something creaking or growling on the other side. It's all in my head, all in my head. There's nothing out there. I crawl around the house, because God forbid, I might see the Void. My body aches. My head, too. The dosimeter kept crackling; I fed it to the Void so it wouldn't distract me. And now I'm completely alone. Just my Self and the Void.”

TOP SECRET 
To the Head of the “Barrier” Project, 
D.Sc., Professor V.M. Chubko. 
December 12, 2006
 
Report on the tests of the “ZX-16” emitter. 
 
The tests were conducted in the “Perimeter Protection” mode under deliberate emergency conditions, which caused the “ZX-16” emitter to overheat. 
 
During the tests, uncontrolled bursts of psi-emission were detected, at its peak it exceeded the calculated parameters of the emitter by 60%, which contradicts Kaymanov’s theory of “overheating of the emitter leads to a decrease in power”. 
 
We assume that overheating causes an increase in the parameters of neural activity of the “I-1M”, turning the pseudomesocephalum from the source of the psi-emission into a repeater. 
 
These unforeseen consequences of the tests allow us to assume that the combination of the emitter and the “I-1M” may provide a more reliable option for the operation of the “Barrier” system than the “Rainbow-1”. 
 
I would also like to inform you that the biomaterials became unusable as a result of these tests, therefore new shipments are required. 
 
To the Head of the ZX-16 Laboratory
PhD in Tech Prikhodko P.S.
December 20, 2006
 
Pavel Stepanovich, these “unforeseen consequences” of yours from the unauthorized tests led to the loss of the biomaterial we acquired with great difficulty. Do you understand the gravity of your actions? 
 
Please refrain from conducting further tests without my permission. I understand your eagerness to outdo your competitors, but don't lose your head. 
 
Speaking of competitors, yesterday they achieved stable operation of their “psychoemotional correctors” with only a single shutdown for cooling off period per day. Your operating model (5 minutes on, 3 minutes off) is incomparable. 
 
However, I do not wish to discourage you. I believe that this “brain” of yours is the future. But! We need the “Barrier” in the present, so we plan to use a completely technological solution from your colleagues at “Rainbow-1” for now. 
 
Continue your research at a moderate pace; you will be notified of new deliveries of biomaterials shortly.

A PDA belonging to an employee of the underground complex beneath Lake Yantar. It contains scans of the documents on the commencement of work on an “artificially grown biological psi-emitter”. 
 
Among the files are data on the supply of biomaterials—feral dogs and wild wolves. The reports, addressed to a certain V.M. Chubko, state that these biomaterials are insufficient for long-term research. In response, an order to search for an alternative source of biomaterials was sent. 
 
Also stored in the device's memory are instructions prescribed by the management, a group photo of the complex's employees celebrating New Year's in the laboratory, and a list of members of the first six-month research shift.
PDA with the “ZX-16” lab evacuation order

PDA of an employee of the underground complex under Lake Yantar. An email marked “URGENT” was sent to its inbox: 
 
“Due to the state of emergency, you are ordered to immediately: 
 
1. Gather four sets of documentation containing reports on the laboratory's activities. Thereafter, destroy the original documents marked “Top Secret”. 
 
2. Dispose of all the biomaterials. 
 
3. Prepare the experimental “Veil” program for uploading into the pseudomesocephalum “I-1M”. 
 
4. Set the laboratory into the power-saving mode and activate the backup power sources. 
 
5. Activate all external tracking sensors. 
 
6. Form four groups in accordance with the emergency instructions. Each group will receive a set of personal protective equipment and a set of documentation. 
 
7. Seal off the laboratory.
 
8. Move to the main laboratory in area Z17-45. 
 
Head of Laboratory “ZX-16”
PhD in Tech Prikhodko P.S. 
April 12, 2007”
PDA of the Head of the “ZX-16” lab

All data on this PDA has been erased, except for one text file titled “Last Will”: 
 
“I humbly ask the finder to forward this letter to my colleagues, to whom I remained loyal till the very end. Colleagues, please notify my loved ones and forward them the letter from my office at the Center. Thank you. 
April 26, 2007
 
I am Pavel Stepanovich Prikhodko, head of the ZX-16 laboratory. Two weeks ago, I’ve ordered the lab to be sealed off. After the disaster, contact with the Center was lost, continuing the work was impossible. 
 
I’ve sent four groups with the priceless results of our endeavors to the Center, at least one of them should reach it. Meanwhile, I’ve stayed behind to upload the “Veil” program into the “I-1M”, which was supposed to instill absolute invisibility and a subconscious reluctance to approach the lab to everyone within a 300-meter radius.
 
I don't know why, but the “Perimeter Defense” program has activated instead. Now, whenever I try to leave the lab, I pass out and awaken in the shielded room.
 
I’ve spent two weeks here, trying to turn off the “brain” and figure out how could it even activate this program? The answer terrifies me. Perhaps my colleagues' most fantastic hypothesis about the self-learning capabilities of “I-1M” was correct. If so, that Monster is probably delighted by my torment.
 
I’ve tried to kill it, but it was useless; the hull is protected by armored glass. The emitter can only be shut down from the backup control panel. I've trapped myself. 
 
I’ve ran out of food and water, and the psi-emission will eventually destroy me as a person, leaving me a brain-dead shell for the few remaining days. I don't want that. So, I kept the last bullet for myself.
 
Farewell, please don't think badly of me.”

Judging by the presence of the maps of the South of the Zone and the geotagged large objects, the owner of this PDA was conducting some kind of reconnaissance of Cordon, Garbage, Dark Valley and the vicinity of the “Agroprom” which ended when the helicopter made an emergency landing with no survivors.

This folder contains a map of Bright Beam, which, in addition to the main buildings, marks the sewer system, a tunnel leading to the Freedom faction’s base, and all fortified positions within the town. 
 
Tucked inside is a remarkable note—part prayer, part offensive order—which offers insight into the unconventional structure of the "Monolith" faction: 
 
“Let us pray, brothers, for we are far from HIS black, blinding radiance. But we hear HIS call, and HE hears our prayers. 
 
Following HIS call, we have fortified ourselves on the outskirts of the city, hidden from the gaze of the infidels that litter the city’s rooftops. But soon we will bring them down from heaven to earth; by HIS command, we will crush the infidels. 
 
My brothers, a great honor is destined for us! To become the enforcers of HIS will, the vanguard of the liberation of this city from the infidels. Our brothers will soon arrive here, and HE has blessed us to make the first step—to make preparations for an offensive through the city’s sewers. 
 
And then, together with our brothers, by HIS will, we will destroy the heretics!”

Deliver in person 
To the head of special regime colony 1269-bis 
K.P. Pakhlo.
 
Dear Kirill Petrovich, I am interested in acquiring one of your inmates, index: 115. Please send his file as soon as possible. We are prepared to pay more than usual, but only after completing the hand-over. Please entrust the transportation of him to us – your people are already under suspicion at the checkpoint. 
May 16, 2005
 
Deliver in person 
To the Head of the "Barrier" Project 
V.M. Chubko.
 
Dear Vadim Mikhailovich, as per your request, I am pleased to provide the information about inmate № 115: Viktor Davidovich Krivoshein, born in 1941. Candidate of Technical Sciences, until 1975 an employee of the Kyiv Research Institute of Clinical and Experimental Surgery. In 1990, he founded the “Gray Brothers” sect. ”We’ve played Gods. And we’ve lost. That's it, finito, the emitter has completely spiraled out of control. We serve its will 22 hours a day, and only when it enters the cooling period do we come to our senses a little. 
 
The goddamn automation is working flawlessly. Glumov must be proud of himself. I feel sorry for him, a terrible death. He tried to shut it down, but fell after taking only a few steps. First, he gouged out his own eyes, then tore out his throat with his bare hands. Even at reduced power, the emitter protects itself, as programmed. 
 
Sobolev suggested destroying the transformer station to deprive the emitter of power. Leonid Dmitrievich shot him on the spot. I get where he’s coming from; we all understand what will happen if it gets shut down. If only Kaymanov was there with us, he’d know what to do. Alas, he never returned from the “Center”. 
 
There is no way out. Or rather, there is, but it’s a very special one. Eventually, the food supply will run out, and the psi-emission outside is so powerful… it's better than wandering around like a scorched, braindead cinder. I've seen enough with our “biomaterial”. 
 
One thing pleases me: we've definitely surpassed that blockhead Prikhodko and his stupid “brain”. Be proud of yourselves, colleagues, and farewell.”

An empty folder marked “Top Secret”, with a note from one of the lab's employees on the inside:

In his words, you keep dragging classified documents up onto the roof, handing out the wrong amounts of neurostimulators, failing to properly shield your facilities, and blaming every single malfunction of your emitter on the cooling system. Yet, your own reports tell a completely different story. 
 
I look forward to seeing you at the tests at the “Center” laboratory; afterward, we’ll head to your complex to celebrate the new year — 2007 — and take the opportunity to go over your reports. 
 
And one last thing: some of your lost, classified documents were recovered from the Polissya Hotel. That’s the second time in six months! I’m well aware that the hotel staff are part of our organization, but please, show some professional responsibility. After all, outsiders do occasionally stay in Pripyat.”

A folder containing documents found in Pripyat. A note on the cover reads: “the last part of the code – 8”. On the inside of the cover, another note reads: “Gunslinger, find me in one of the houses on the outskirts of Bright Beam. Hurry up. Journalist”.
 
Inside the folder, alongside documents detailing experiments at the “Center” Laboratory, consisting entirely of numbers and convoluted scientific jargon, lies an old notebook containing personal entries:
 
” Strange place they chose for the installations. The soil is completely unusable and terribly radioactive. We had to wear NBC suits, which are usually worn by Chernobyl personnel, to avoid grabbing a large dose. Even now, sitting in the break room, I can’t bring myself to eat the food they serve here. It's a good thing no one's gonna bother you here.
 
Vadim Mikhailovich gave a full tour of the central laboratory. He described the working principle of the plant and its objectives. The sheer scale of it is truly mesmerizing, and my emitter is no match for it. It hardly matters that it’s named after me. 
 
 I was particularly struck by its surface generators. We were not allowed to get close to them - the background radiation near them is just off the scale.: it’s terrifying to think about what will happen to those currently calibrating these machines — or to their descendants.
 
Vadim Mikhailovich demonstrated the installation in operation. It required ten staff members, himself included, to be connected to it. He boasted that he was about to “grab God by the beard”. Well, this time, he didn't just grab it — he ripped it out by the roots. 
 
Quite the New Year’s gift. By mid-March, they plan to fully launch the “Center” installation. It’s impossible to imagine what the consequences of all this might be. Perhaps 2007 will be the last New Year humanity will ever celebrate.”

An old yellowed notebook with notes from the first military expeditions to the Zone. Most of the pages are bloodstained or missing altogether. 
 
March 15, 2007. The evacuation of civilians from the village took longer than the military leadership had originally anticipated. We're missing five residents, all of them well into their sixties. According to eyewitness accounts, an hour after the “incident” the old folk just took off northward. Major strictly forbade to send a group after them...
 
March 16, 2007. We reached a graveyard of radioactive machinery. Along the way, we’ve lost two armored vehicles. The first one somehow veered into a ditch, and all its electronics failed right then and there. The second one suddenly stalled in the middle of the road and wouldn't start again. Among the officers, there’re talks that the enemy is using electromagnetic weapons to disable our equipment. The question is: what kind of enemy are we dealing with?
 
March 19, 2007. Major has completely lost his mind: he wants to hold his ground in the city and wait for reinforcements. Communication with the military command is impossible — the radio is dead. Vasilyev has been tinkering with it for two hours now; he’s already been severely reprimanded for his careless handling of government property. A scouting party headed north toward an old military base. Word is, there might be survivors there. 
 
March 21, 2007. We’ve found Vasilyev. He had locked himself inside a room on the second floor of a house and hanged himself. The scouts still haven’t returned — Major is already planning to send more men after them. Vasyan suggested we volunteer. He said we could take a detour and reach the Perimeter. I’ve agreed.

A personal diary belonging to a stalker-hunter, containing some rather curious notes about bloodsuckers: 
 
”November 9th, 2011: I was keeping an eye on the Bull's group from a distance. People who know better steer clear of this place, but the big guy decided to lead his rookies right through the village — as if he didn't know what lived there, the fool. 
 
They walked around the water tower, reached a low spot between two hills, and stumbled upon several mangled corpses. While Bull was trying to calm the panicking rookies, the mutant crept up behind him and sank its tentacles right into his neck. Upon seeing the creature, the rookies bolted straight into a field of anomalies, leaving their “mentor” to die. 
 
The lesson here? Don't take rookies north of the Garbage. And know thy enemy. 
 
November 30th, 2011: Bloodsuckers thrive in high humidity and darkness, which is why they prefer to inhabit cellars and basements. I’ve made it a habit to toss a couple of grenades into such places before heading down myself — have already taken out a few of the beasts that way. 
 
The slime they secrete dries out quickly, even at room temperature, so it’s no wonder these creatures avoid the sunlight. They don't like rain either—presumably because it makes them easier to spot. 
 
December 14th, 2011: I spoke with the professors at the camp and shared my observations (for a fee, of course). A new team of zoologists has just arrived, and they’re quite keen on the local fauna. They were particularly fascinated by the bloodsuckers' tentacles. 
 
Just imagine—they’ve only ever seen these creatures in pieces or preserved in formalin, yet they’ve already cooked up a whole slew of theories, each one more elaborate than the last! One moment they’re claiming the tentacles are sensory organs—like a snake’s tongue—and the next, they’re insisting that one of them is actually a reproductive organ… 
 
Honestly, I got tired of listening to these “experts”, so I struck a deal with them. I’ll bring back a few specimens—who knows, maybe I’ll end up a bit richer, and they’ll finally stop spouting such nonsense.”

You’ve saved my hide once again, Gunslinger. Honestly, I’ve lost count of how many times that’s happened now. And once again, you’ve vanished. I couldn’t reach you over the comms, so I’m leaving this note. 
 
Word has it that the military has started showing up here, dealing with Rat. After what happened with our joint business in the Valley, it’s best to steer clear of them. I’ve decided to leave this hideout and head North. I’d advise you to do the same, though knowing you, you’ll probably just brush that off. 
 
The documents we recovered in the Valley shed some light on things. It turns out there really were secret laboratories in the Zone, though what’s become of them now is anyone’s guess. It’s possible some are still operational — if so, we need to find them. Unfortunately, I don’t have any more details; the eggheads over at Yantar couldn’t tell me anything concrete — they don’t know much themselves. 
 
By the way, if you get the chance, pay a visit to an old acquaintance of ours in the Swamps. He asked me to let you know that he’s managed to get hold of the medical supplies you were looking for. Just be careful—the psi-emission there is off the charts following the last blowout. 
 
 Take care of yourself—for the Zone’s sake. 
Journalist
